candidates.title: U.S. rail traffic up 7.8% as intermodal leads gainers
candidates.excerpt: U.S. rail traffic increased 7.8% in the week ended Oct. 24 compared with the same week in 2025, as growth in intermodal shipments outpaced gains in carloads, Association of American Railroads data shows. Weekly intermodal volume, which includes containers and trailers, rose 11.3%, while carload traffic increased 3.6%. Both measures grew faster than their respective year-to-date rates. Eight of the 10 carload commodity groups recorded year-over-year increases. Petroleum and petroleum products led percentage growth, rising 15.4%, followed by motor vehicles and parts at 15.3%. Forest products increased 11.7%, and metallic ores and metals gained 11.6%. Farm products excluding grain, and food fell 3.7%, while grain posted a rare decline at 1.4%. For the first 42 weeks of 2026, combined U.S. rail traffic increased 3.8% from the same period in 2025. Carloads rose 2.7%, while intermodal traffic was better by 4.7%. candidates.title: 9 alleged Mexican Cartel associates arrested in California train theft ring
candidates.excerpt: Nine men allegedly connected to Mexico’s Sinaloa Cartel have been arrested in Southern California following a yearlong investigation into an organized cargo theft operation that targeted BNSF Railway trains and resulted in millions of dollars in stolen merchandise, authorities said. The San Bernardino County Sheriff’s Department announced Wednesday that its Rural Crime Task Force arrested the nine suspects Oct. 16 during a search of a residence in San Bernardino. Investigators said the suspects were part of a coordinated criminal network connected to the Sinaloa Cartel that had been burglarizing BNSF Railway trains over the past 12 months. The investigation uncovered an operation involving numerous suspects and vehicles used to steal merchandise from rail shipments, according to the Sheriff’s Department. candidates.title: Trinity reports higher railcar orders, tightening leasing market
candidates.excerpt: DALLAS — New freight car deliveries will bottom out this year, Trinity Industries executives said today while announcing third-quarter financial results. “In Rail Products, deliveries increased 29% sequentially and orders exceeded deliveries … A shrinking fleet and fewer railcars in storage point to a tightening market, and we believe 2026 will mark the cyclical low point for industry deliveries,” CEO Jean Savage said. October marked the 17th straight month that the North American freight car fleet shrank. Eighteen percent of freight cars were in storage, Trinity said, which is the lowest reading since May 2023. “This year, we’re talking about 40,000 cars being scrapped and less than 25,000 new cars being built. So the market is staying very tight overall,” Savage said on the company’s earnings call. candidates.title: Schneider to shift intermodal business to Norfolk Southern
candidates.excerpt: ATLANTA — Schneider, the No. 3 domestic intermodal company, will shift its freight to Norfolk Southern in the East. The move, announced today and effective Jan. 1, comes amid changing intermodal alliances. J.B. Hunt, the largest intermodal provider, has been sending more volume to CSX in the East over the past year due to the expansion of BNSF-CSX interline intermodal service. candidates.title: CSX operations returning to normal after technology systems outage
candidates.excerpt: JACKSONVILLE, Fla. — CSX operations are returning to normal today after a technology systems outage disrupted service beginning Tuesday morning. CSX said core functions have returned to many of its most critical railroad applications, and that it is once again interchanging traffic with other Class I railroads. Intermodal terminal gates are functional and auto and Transflo terminals are operational, as are customer resources including the ShipCSX shipper portal. RailState, which monitors freight traffic using a network of trackside sensors, says the railroad’s operations ramped up overnight. “CSX freight traffic fell 46% against its 30-day average for 29 hours and is back at normal,” RailState told Trains this morning. From midnight to 8 a.m. today, RailState’s sensors counted 162 freight trains — well above the 138 that would be typical. candidates.title: South Carolina recycling business closed over alleged possession of stolen railroad materials
candidates.excerpt: CHERAW, S.C. — A South Carolina recycling business has been shut down after officers executing a search warrant found thousands of pounds of stolen CSX Transportation materials. Cheraw Iron and Metal Inc. has been closed until further notice following execution of the search warrant on Tuesday, Oct. 27, by the Chesterfield County Sheriff’s Office, with assistance from the South Carolina Law Enforcement Division, its Immigration Unit, and CSX police. A press release from the Sheriff’s Office said the search warrant was obtained following an investigation into thefts from CSX and Sandhill Telephone Co., as well as other thefts reported in the county. Officers found that materials purchased by Cheraw Iron and Metal included track, spikes, and other CSX materials, as well as wiring believed to have been stolen from Sandhill Telephone. candidates.title: BLET ratifies agreement for CPKC’s DM&E workers
candidates.excerpt: INDEPENDENCE, Ohio — Members of the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers and Trainmen have ratified a new five-year agreement with CPKC covering its Dakota, Minnesota & Eastern lines, the union has announced. The agreement will create parity between workers on the DM&E and those on CPKC’s former Soo Line territory. It includes a increase in the hourly rate for engineers of 41.42%, compounded, over the life of the agreement, along with increases of 32.63% for conductors and brakemen, the union said when the tentative agreement was announced [see “BLET, CPKC reach tentative agreement …,” Trains.com, Oct. 1, 2026]. The deal also includes increased meal allowances, greater flexibility for personal leave days, and new work-rule protections. — To report news or errors, contact trainsnewswire@firecrown.com. candidates.title: Maersk lowers intermodal fuel fees in Italy
candidates.excerpt: Maersk will reduce its Intermodal Fuel Fee percentages for truck and RCO movements in Italy. The revised levels will apply equally to import and export services from a Price Calculation Date (PCD) of 1 November 2026. The truck surcharge will decrease from 18% to 17%. Meanwhile, the RCO surcharge will fall from 9% to 8%. Unlike the previous update, the effective date will be the same for FMC and non-FMC shipments. For non-FMC shipments, the PCD is the scheduled departure date of the first water leg at booking confirmation. For FMC shipments, it is the final container gate-in date for non-SPOT bookings. Maersk will continue to review the surcharge levels monthly. The carrier said further revisions may be required as energy market conditions change.

candidates.title: Hapag-Lloyd introduces Pakistan–UAE reefer surcharge
candidates.excerpt: Hapag-Lloyd will introduce a Peak Season Surcharge (PSS) on refrigerated cargo moving from Pakistan to selected ports in the United Arab Emirates. The surcharge will apply to sailings commencing from 1 November 2026. It will remain valid until 15 November 2026. The origin scope covers Karachi and Port Qasim in Pakistan. The UAE destinations are Khor Fakkan, Sharjah, Fujairah, Umm Al Quwain, Ras Al Khaimah and Ajman.

The new port will be located west of Tanger Med 2 and will include 1,200 metres of quay. The development will add annual handling capacity of 4.5 million containers. Planned investment in the project amounts to 8 billion Moroccan dirhams. The project will also support the ongoing expansion of Tanger Med’s passenger and roll-on/roll-off facilities. In addition, it will enable the eastern extension of Tanger Med 2. Once the new projects are completed, the Tanger Med complex could reach total annual capacity of 20 million containers. candidates.title: Contship Jet sinks after drone attack in Black Sea, all 18 crew rescued
candidates.excerpt: The Liberian-flagged containership Contship Jet has sunk in the Black Sea after being struck by three maritime drones off the Bulgarian coast on 28 October, with all 18 crew members successfully rescued, according to Bulgarian authorities. The sinking was confirmed on 29 October by the Varna Regional Administration, citing information from maritime traffic control and the Bulgarian Maritime Administration. The vessel was travelling from Haifa, Israel, to Constanța, Romania, carrying 421 containers when the attack occurred near Cape Kaliakra. According to the Bulgarian Ministry of Transport and Communications, the Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre in Constanța received notification of the attack at 12:01 local time on 28 October, approximately 17 nautical miles east of Cape Kaliakra. The crew abandoned the vessel at 12:13, prompting an immediate search-and-rescue operation involving three Bulgarian Navy vessels and a Border Police vessel. candidates.title: Same Trade Lane, Different Footprint: Carrier Emissions Intensity Differs by Up to 35% on Major Container Routes
candidates.excerpt: Same Trade Lane, Different Footprint: Carrier Emissions Intensity Differs by Up to 35% on Major Container Routes The report also shows why absolute emissions are a poor measure of efficiency. On the China/East Asia–Northern Europe trade, the carrier with the lowest emissions intensity, out of the three carriers examined, also recorded the highest average emissions per voyage, highlighting the importance of cargo volumes and vessel utilization when assessing environmental performance. Based on an analysis of 83,817 voyages performed by 6,730 container-carrying vessels, the report examines how actual vessel operations, including sailing patterns, port stays, cargo utilization and vessel deployment, influence maritime emissions performance. The findings highlight the importance of looking beyond aggregate figures to understand the operational conditions shaping transportation efficiency. candidates.title: Non-bank NAV lending margins widen despite fund finance pricing pressure
candidates.excerpt: Non-bank NAV lending margins widen despite fund finance pricing pressure Non-bank lenders are charging increasingly higher margins on complex net asset value (NAV) facilities despite wider pricing compression across the fund finance market, according to a new report from Corpay Private Markets. The fifth edition of the firm’s Lender Book Report found that average non-bank NAV lending margins widened from 756 basis points in February 2025 to 794 basis points in August 2026. By contrast, average bank NAV margins narrowed from 447 to 435 basis points over the same period. This comes as the fund finance lender base continues to diversify, with alternative credit providers accounting for around 30 per cent of lenders tracked by Corpay’s Alpha Match platform, up from roughly 25 per cent three years ago. candidates.excerpt: Police recovered approximately $54,000 in stolen Hot Wheels merchandise following a freight train burglary in Colton, California. A witness called 911 around 3 a.m. Thursday, October 22, reporting suspicious activity near railroad tracks. Officers spotted a black Chevrolet Silverado leaving the area and initiated a traffic stop. The investigation ended with one arrest and 350 boxes of toy cars in police custody. According to video released by the Colton Police Department, the caller reported people stealing merchandise near Maple Street. An officer positioned himself near Seventh Street and La Cadena Drive while monitoring the surrounding roads. Footage shows authorities following the pickup before stopping its driver. The man exited with his hands on his head, and officers took him into custody. The department confirmed the recovery in its October 22 Facebook announcement.
